title: Adaptive hedging and per-tenant slowpath cooldown to reduce 5xx/timeouts during customer escalations
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
During a customer escalation window we observed a cluster of 5xx errors and long-tail timeouts originating from a slow downstream model artifact fetch (model shard registry) that caused streaming responses to stall at the proxy layer. Standard retry logic amplified load and led to tenant-visible error spikes.

Goal:
- Implement a conservative, per-tenant adaptive cooldown plus controlled hedging (parallel request hedging) that reduces visible 5xx/timeouts while avoiding retry amplification and duplicate-cost blowups for customers.

Proposal (high level):
1) Short-circuit: Detect requests that hit a slowpath (proxy saw no bytes for X ms during streaming handshake) and mark the tenant request fingerprint as "slowpath:pending" for a short window (default 30s). While marked, new incoming requests for that tenant follow a degraded fastpath: lower concurrency, strict per-tenant admission, and route to cached model variants or regional fallbacks.
2) Hedging: For requests that exceed latency threshold T_hedge (2000ms) without any bytes, dispatch a hedged request to a compatible model variant/region with a soft deduplication window of 1500ms. Use idempotency tokens (client-provided or generated by edge) to prevent dual side-effects for mutating endpoints (function calls / tool integrations).
3) Diagnostics: Add X-RW-DIAG headers to hedged/slowpath requests capturing request-fingerprint, tenant-id-hash, and hedging decision timestamp to correlate traces across services and to drive automated root-cause grouping in the console.
4) Billing controls: Expose a per-tenant hedging budget (tokens per minute) and default to conservative counts to avoid unexpected billing increases.

Trade-offs considered:
- Duplicate token consumption vs. customer-visible latency: hedging reduces visible errors but causes duplicate token usage; mitigation via low default hedging budget and opt-out flag for high-cost tenants.
- Complexity of idempotency enforcement vs. engineering velocity: when an idempotency token is absent, we fall back to read-only hedging only; write-like calls use a single-request cooldown path.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Reduce tenant-visible 5xx rate by >= 60% in post-deploy canary for tenants that previously experienced slowpath spikes (30d baseline).
- Limit hedged duplicate token usage to < 5% of served tokens in canary cohort.
- Console support: trace links surface X-RW-DIAG correlation and a new "slowpath events" panel per-tenant.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev -> dogfood): implement runtime flags, unit/integration tests, and end-to-end canary with internal tenants.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable hedging + cooldown for 5 alpha tenants with hedging budget 2/min and close monitoring on cost dashboards.
- Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 10% of hosted traffic over 48h with automated rollback triggers on token-cost/correctness regressions.
- Phase 3 (global): default on with conservative hedging budgets and PM/CS opt-out controls for customers.
